items.title: Transient CB2R modulation durably restricts breast cancer plasticity by stabilizing a luminal like cell identity
items.author: María Salazar-Roa
items.content: We investigate how transient cannabinoid receptor 2 modulation influences breast cancer cell plasticity. We show that transient CB2R modulation durably stabilizes a luminal-like state, reducing tumor-initiating capacity and improving tamoxifen sensitivity

items.title: ALDH2 inhibition reprograms tubular epithelial cell metabolism and promotes renal injury susceptibility
items.author: Yuguo Chen
items.content: ALDH2 acts as a mediator of fatty acid oxidation (FAO) in tubular epithelial cells (TECs). ALDH2 inhibition triggers FAO dysfunction via downregulation of the PPARα/RXRα-CPT1α pathway and contributes to renal fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD).

items.title: Impaired protein translation inhibits DNA replication by a Claspin-Chk1-Rif1 pathway
items.author: Raimundo Freire
items.content: Characterisation of the response to protein synthesis inhibition identifies a Claspin/Chk1/Rif1 pathway that couples translational attenuation to suppression of DNA replication.

items.title: GATA3 and YBX1 are associated with ER-specific metabolic programs and vulnerabilities in breast cancer
items.author: Mohammad Askandar Iqbal
items.content: Integrative transcriptomic, single-cell and functional analyses identify GATA3 and YBX1 as estrogen receptor-specific regulators linking metabolic reprogramming to therapeutic vulnerability in breast cancer.

items.title: Functional mapping of IFITM3 resolves its antiviral core and deciphers human influenza susceptibility
items.author: Min Zheng
items.content: This study generates a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants using deep mutational scanning. The resulting map resolves the protein’s intramembrane antiviral core and identifies key rare human alleles that dictate susceptibility to influenza infection

items.title: Drosophila UBE3A regulates substrates associated with gliopathic seizures through direct ubiquitination of translation initiation and ubiquitin-proteasome proteins
items.author: Lawrence T. Reiter
items.content: An in vivo Drosophila UBAIT approach identifies neuronal and glial Dube3a substrates, implicating glial RNA-processing pathways as potential contributors to seizure phenotypes in Dup15q syndrome.

items.title: Synaptic-level organization of long-range cholinergic circuits in the basal forebrain
items.author: Xiangning Li
items.content: Whole-brain distribution of presynaptic terminals of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons was acquired via fMOST imaging, revealing their heterogeneous organizational patterns.

items.title: Targeting Artemis sensitizes acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells to topoisomerase 2 poisons by disrupting DNA-PKcs-dependent repair
items.author: Nicholas R. Pannunzio
items.content: Artemis is a critical mediator of topoisomerase IIA adduct processing and DNA double-strand break repair. Inhibiting Artemis or DNA-PKcs sensitizes B-cell ALL to Top2 poisons, revealing a therapeutic strategy to improve treatment efficacy.
